links.outcome: Overall diagnostic accuracy of ChatGPT-5 versus general dentists on periapical radiographs
links.effect: ChatGPT-5 overall accuracy 54.0%-63.2% was significantly lower than general dentists 76.0%-85.6% (p < 0.001).
links.quote: Overall accuracy (54.0%-63.2%) was significantly lower than that of general dentists (76.0%-85.6%) (p < 0.001).

links.outcome: Sensitivity of ChatGPT-5 for detecting obturation errors, voids, and periapical lesions on radiographs
links.effect: Low sensitivity for short (13.7%) or long (0.0%) obturations, voids (9.0%-22.7%), and periapical lesions (10.5%-28.6%); high specificity up to 99.3%.
links.quote: ChatGPT-5 demonstrated high specificity (up to 99.3%) for normal or adequately treated findings but low sensitivity for short (13.7%) or long (0.0%) obturations, voids (9.0%-22.7%), and periapical lesions (10.5%-28.6%).

screen.reason: Evaluates diagnostic accuracy of a multimodal foundation model (ChatGPT-5) on dental radiographs compared to clinicians and ground truth, without testing a specific implementation guardrail or deployment practice.
